name: How Can I Compare Kitchen Countertop Allowances in Different Estimates?

mainEntity.name: What countertop details must match when comparing kitchen remodeling estimates?
mainEntity.text: What countertop details must match when comparing kitchen remodeling estimates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Countertop allowances are comparable only when they cover the same material and fabrication requirements. Record the material type, thickness, color or grade, estimated square footage, edge profile, backsplash height, sink cutout, cooktop cutout, seams, supports, templating, delivery, installation, and disposal. Confirm whether the allowance is based on a supplier quote or a broad per-square-foot assumption. Ask whether the contractor includes slab overage, remnants, waterfall ends, full-height backsplash, sink mounting, faucet drilling, seam placement, and reinforcement for overhangs. A proposal may list countertops but omit fabrication, tear-out, plumbing reconnection, or repairs to cabinets that support the surface. Confirm who chooses the supplier and who handles measurement corrections. Use the same countertop material and dimensions in each estimate or request revised pricing after selections are made. If the slab is not yet chosen, ask for a realistic allowance and the exact adjustment formula. Record credits, markups, and approval deadlines. This comparison prevents a low initial total from becoming materially higher once fabrication details and installation requirements are known.
acceptedAnswer.description: Match countertop material, thickness, slab grade, square footage, edge profile, sink cutout, backsplash, templating, installation, delivery, seams, support, and disposal. Ask whether the allowance covers overage and remnants. A lower countertop allowance may omit fabrication or installation costs.
